hlni.insight: A short illustrative activity can reveal where you need help or what you want to investigate next; it cannot determine which degree suits you.
hlni.audienceGap: Belief that degree fit is a universal feeling rather than a researchable question.
hlni.viewerChange: Learns to use specific sticking points as questions for course teams.
hlni.support: The observation belongs to this activity and participant; it supports a next question rather than a general prediction.
hlni.payoff: The student identifies a specific logical uncertainty instead of worrying about the overall degree label.

creativeAngle: Using sample tasks to identify specific learning needs rather than guessing degree fit.
objective: Help students shift from vague degree comparison to asking concrete questions.
targetAudience: +2 students seeking accessible, supportive guidance, including students worried about marks, confidence, or belonging

shots.name: The Peer Pressure
shots.visual: Two students sitting in a library looking stressed at their laptops.
shots.dialogue: Everyone says BBA is for leaders and B.Com is for accountants.
shots.cameraPerformance: Close-up on the student's doubtful expression.

shots.name: The Vague Assumption
shots.visual: Student sighs and closes their laptop tab.
shots.dialogue: I feel stuck just guessing which one fits me better.
shots.onscreenText: Is it just a gut feeling?
shots.cameraPerformance: Mid-shot showing the student looking overwhelmed.

shots.name: The Shared Task
shots.visual: A friend slides a piece of paper over to the student.
shots.dialogue: Don't guess. Try this sample task instead.
shots.cameraPerformance: Focus shifts from the laptop to the paper.

shots.name: The Illustrative Activity
shots.visual: Close-up on the paper showing a specific calculation problem.
shots.dialogue: Example: Task: Calculate the cost-volume-profit break-even point.
shots.onscreenText: Example: Task: Calculate the cost-volume-profit break-even point.
shots.cameraPerformance: Camera zooms in on the text on the paper.

shots.name: The Concrete Question
shots.visual: Student points to a specific line on the paper and writes a note.
shots.dialogue: I'm stuck on this part. Can you explain the logic for categorizing fixed overheads?
shots.onscreenText: Can you explain the logic for categorizing fixed overheads?
shots.cameraPerformance: Student looks relieved, smiling at the specific question.

shots.name: The Next Step
shots.visual: Student circles their question, then looks at the camera.
shots.dialogue: Use these specific questions to talk with course teams.
shots.cameraPerformance: Direct eye contact with the viewer.

productionNotes.editing: Tight cuts between the problem and the task.

creativeSummary.keyCreativeIdea: Transforming degree comparison from abstract labels into researchable questions through specific sample tasks.
shootingPriority: The reaction to finding a specific sticking point

storySpine.startingBelief: Choosing a degree is a 'gut feeling' and friends' opinions are facts.
storySpine.studentSituation: Student feels pressure from a peer's confident degree choice.
storySpine.observation: Friend's 'certainty' is based on a single illustrative activity.
storySpine.focus: Separating personal activity preferences from degree requirements.
storySpine.whyQuestionFollows: One task cannot reveal the breadth of a full degree programme.
storySpine.changedAction: Student and friend both try a sample task and record where they need help.
storySpine.visibleConsequence: Friend admits they are stuck on a specific detail, not the whole degree.
storySpine.channelExperience: A supportive, honest conversation about clarifying personal academic needs.

selected.title: The Honest Task Journal
selected.audienceGap: Belief that degree fit is a universal feeling rather than a researchable question.
selected.hlni: A short illustrative activity can reveal where you need help or what you want to investigate next; it cannot determine which degree suits you.
selected.viewerChange: Learns to use specific sticking points as questions for course teams.
selected.concept: Recording specific help-needs while trying illustrative tasks.
selected.device: A shared notebook for task-sticking points.
selected.support: The observation belongs to this activity and participant; it supports a next question rather than a general prediction.
methodSteps: Try or inspect a clearly illustrative task.
Record one point where you needed help and one question you want to investigate.
Turn the observation into a question for a real course brief or course team.
selected.interpretationRule: Use the recorded observation to choose the next question, not to select a degree from one activity.
selected.visibleProof: A person records a specific sticking point and asks a different, more useful question afterward.
selected.payoff: Viewer feels empowered to ask questions rather than compare labels.
selected.limitations: A brief exercise does not measure aptitude, learning style, long-term interest or academic performance.
